newsitem.title: UK: Trans-world spat highlights risk in emerging marke.
newsitem.headline: Trans-world spat highlights risk in emerging marke.

text.p: The current dispute between some Russian officials and big metals exporter Trans-World Group highlights the risks involved for Western countries looking to position themselves in the major emerging markets, European emerging market specialists Merchant International Group said.
Trans-World's problems come less than a month after Bre-X ran into difficulties in Indonesia with Busang.

"It...is indicative of a much wider battle which has still to be fought - the struggle for the huge pot of gold expected from rapid growth in the "big" emerging markets - China, India, Russia, Indonesia and Brazil," Merchant International said.
In February, Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov called for more control over foreign participation in the aluminium industry.
Trans-World, which owns a substantial stake in Russian aluminium production, responded last week with an open letter slamming Russia's "craven, political power play."
Merchant International said problems arise when distributing the profits from Western investment and technology in the mineral-rich major emerging markets.

"The Western company feels that having shouldered all the commercial risk it should be proportionately recompensed. However, the host nation views the picture differently, believing its input, whether a market or mineral deposits, warrants tha lion share of the rewards," it said.
Traditionally, in Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East the multi-national company, backed by political pressure from its home government, can force the host government to correct problems.
"However, Russia, China, India and Indonesia are not banana republics or tinpot regimes - they are geo-political heavyweights to which only the EU and the U.S. can be compared," it added.
In coming years the global giants will not be those who throw walls of cash at the big emerging markets.

"Rather, they will be the companies which skilfully play these highly distorted playing fields, signposting specific threats such as corruption, bureaucracy, and unfair market competition, while maximising access to markets and resources through shrewd alliances and/or joint ventures," Merchant International said. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
